prompt: Some people prefer hobbies that involve the use of technology, while others enjoy hobbies that do not require any technological devices. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay:
Some people enjoy hobbies in their free time that use technology, whereas others spend their free time on activities that are not technological. In my view, both are valuable. Technological hobbies are fine in moderation, but people also need offline hobbies so that they do not become addicted.

Most technological hobbies do not require physical movement such as standing or running, and some

individuals become addicted to them with very little physical activity. As a result, this can lead to both physical and mental problems. Physically, it can lead to obesity if they do not eat healthily. Mentally, some individuals may develop anxiety because they feel stressed by video games or are bullied online. This is why offline hobbies such as sport or reading are important, as they balance screen time and keep people physically and mentally healthy.

However, some technological hobbies involve physical movement. For example, virtual-reality games involve a significant amount of movement and burn calories while being fun. Moreover, if someone is bullied while playing, they can simply mute or block the bully and never see them again. Online games also allow people to make friends from different countries, which can be especially valuable for those who find socialising in person difficult. Hobbies such as video editing or coding can also teach useful skills that may later lead to a career.

In conclusion, both types of hobbies have value. Technological hobbies can be social, useful and even physically active, but they should be balanced with offline activities to prevent addiction and protect people's health.
